title: Security & Intrusion
description: What is probing the cluster, what CrowdSec made of it, and which requests were refused. Read the coverage-gaps panel at the bottom before trusting a quiet day.

panels.title: Scenario overflows (24h)
panels.description: An overflow is CrowdSec deciding a threshold was crossed — the closest thing here to "an attack was detected". Detection only: infra/crowdsec runs with no bouncer, so nothing was blocked.

panels.title: Active alerts
panels.description: [may-be-empty] From the CrowdSec LAPI. Zero is the normal state.

panels.title: Parser failure rate
panels.description: The canary nobody thinks to watch. If Traefik's log format changes, CrowdSec silently stops matching and this dashboard goes quiet — which looks exactly like 'no attacks'. Anything sustained above ~1% means the parser, not the internet, went quiet.

panels.title: Rate-limit trips (429)
panels.description: [may-be-empty] Traefik's edge rate limiter firing — 159 trips in the last 7 days, but often none for hours at a stretch. Buckets key on CF-Connecting-IP, so these attribute to a source cleanly ONLY on the Cloudflare path: every direct/tailnet client shares one bucket, and a direct-path client can dodge bucketing entirely by inventing the header.

panels.title: Scenario activity
panels.description: Buckets filling, by scenario. These are the collections installed in infra/crowdsec: crowdsecurity/traefik, http-cve, base-http-scenarios.

panels.title: Overflows by scenario
panels.description: [may-be-empty] The subset that actually crossed a threshold.

panels.title: Top detected source IPs
panels.description: Pulled out of the CrowdSec log line at query time. source_ip is deliberately NOT a Loki label — it is the entire internet — so it is re-extracted here with | regexp, which costs no series.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (source_ip) (count_over_time({cluster="$cluster", app="crowdsec"} |= "performed" | regexp "Ip (?P<source_ip>\\S+) performed" [$__range])))

panels.title: CrowdSec detections
panels.description: [may-be-empty] The raw detection lines, carrying the source IP and the scenario. This is the detail the metrics deliberately cannot hold.

panels.title: HTTP attack surface — from the Traefik access log
Refused and failed requests by status
Known-bad path probes
panels.description: [may-be-empty] Requests for things that do not exist here and never did: /.env, WordPress, phpMyAdmin, /.git, /vendor. Nothing legitimate asks for these, so any non-zero line is somebody walking the URL space.

panels.title: Top source IPs by 4xx
panels.description: ClientHost is already the real client IP: infra/traefik sets forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs for the pod and node CIDRs, so Traefik resolves it through the cloudflared and klipper-lb hops rather than logging the internal address.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (ClientHost) (count_over_time({cluster="$cluster", app="traefik", DownstreamStatus=~"4.."} | json ClientHost="ClientHost" [$__range])))

panels.title: Top 404 paths
panels.description: What people are looking for and not finding. RequestPath includes the query string.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (RequestPath) (count_over_time({cluster="$cluster", app="traefik", DownstreamStatus="404"} | json RequestPath="RequestPath" [$__range])))

panels.title: Top user agents on 4xx
panels.description: Scanners rarely bother to disguise themselves. A recognisable tool name here is a free identification.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (request_User_Agent) (count_over_time({cluster="$cluster", app="traefik", DownstreamStatus=~"4.."} | json [$__range])))

panels.title: Authelia failures and regulation bans
panels.description: [may-be-empty] BEST-EFFORT, not exact. auth/authelia sets no log.format, so its logs ship as unstructured text and these are regex matches over raw lines. Setting `log.format: json` in auth/authelia/templates/configuration.yaml would make this precise — it is a separate change because it touches the auth service.

targets.expr: sum(rate({cluster="$cluster", app="authelia"} |~ "(?i)(authentication failed|invalid credentials|user not found)"[5m]))

panels.title: Requests to the un-gated webhook
panels.description: [may-be-empty] sms-relay's /api/v1/inbound is the one public POST endpoint with no forward-auth — it authenticates by HMAC over the body instead, on its own Ingress specifically to escape Authelia. A rise in non-2xx here is signature failures, i.e. someone poking it.

options.content:
Every HTTP panel above is built on the Traefik access log, which is **complete coverage of external HTTP by construction** — every ingress route is pinned to the `websecure` entrypoint by the `infra/ingress-policy` admission policy, so nothing can quietly route around it.

That guarantee stops at HTTP. These paths never touch Traefik and are **invisible here**:

| Path | Exposure | What is missing |
|---|---|---|
| **Minecraft `:25565`** | Public, via the VPS haproxy relay | No request log at all. The relay does not preserve source IP, so even the VPS log cannot attribute a connection. Access control is the Minecraft whitelist. |
| **Jellyfin** | Public, via the VPS Caddy relay → NodePort `:30096` | Caddy's access log stays on the VPS and is not shipped. No rate limit, no CrowdSec. Auth is Jellyfin accounts. |
| **headlamp `:30100`** | NodePort, LAN/tailnet only | No ingress, no logging. The ServiceAccount behind it is **cluster-admin** — the login page is the only gate. |

Two further caveats on what *is* shown:

- **429s attribute to a source only on the Cloudflare path.** The rate limiter buckets on `CF-Connecting-IP`; direct (tailnet/LAN) clients have no such header and therefore share a single bucket.
- **CrowdSec blocks nothing.** `infra/crowdsec` runs deliberately without a bouncer — the Traefik plugin fetches from `plugins.traefik.io` at pod start, which would turn a routine Traefik restart into an ingress outage. Everything here is detection.

A quiet dashboard means *nothing was detected on the paths that are watched*. Check the **parser failure rate** stat above before reading it as "nothing happened".
